reasoning_traces.think:
The RAG evaluation score E_{\text{RAG}} is defined as a normalized combination of recall and precision over retrieved documents relative to ground-truth answers. It is computed via E_{\text{RAG}} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{recall} + \text{precision}). Citation scoring kernel K_{\text{cite}} evaluates document-query relevance using a learned similarity metric. These primitives form a dual structure where E_{\text{RAG}} acts as an upper bound on K_{\text{cite}}, ensuring that high-quality retrievals support accurate citations. The AI Ops Autonomy Index A_{\text{ops}} integrates learning efficiency L_{\text{learn}} and cost reduction C_{\text{cost}} into a single scalar, reflecting how much GSE can self-optimize without external input. Failure modes include E_{\text{RAG}} dropping below 0.5 due to hallucination or poor retrieval, or A_{\text{ops}} falling below 0.3 when system dependencies exceed acceptable thresholds.
